searches.query: My tent seam separated during normal use 18 months after purchase. What do I need for a manufacturing-warranty assessment, and is a cash refund guaranteed?

chunks.text: Tent manufacturing warranty  Tents have a 24-month warranty for manufacturing defects, beginning on the purchase date. A stitching seam that separates during normal use can qualify. The customer must provide proof of purchase and clear photos so the repair team can assess the failure. The warranty team chooses repair or replacement after assessment; support cannot promise a cash refund before that decision.  Damage from animals, sharp objects, storms beyond the tent's rating, ordinary fabric wear, or incorrect storage is outside this warranty. Accidental damage can still be sent for a paid repair assessment. A quotation must be approved before paid repair work starts. The repair-price guide lists the fixed fees that are currently published; some repairs require an individual quote.  Customers should dry a tent before packing it for inspection. Do not include fuel canisters, batteries, food, or personal belongings. An approved manufacturing-defect claim receives a prepaid ground label.

Outlet and final-sale products  Products marked final sale in the outlet cannot be returned merely because the customer changes their mind, chooses the wrong color, or finds a lower price later. The final-sale marking appears on the product page and the order confirmation. A general store promotion does not make a product final sale unless the product is specifically marked that way.  Final sale does not remove the manufacturing warranty. A defective outlet tent follows the tent warranty assessment process, including proof of purchase and photos. Cosmetic wear that was disclosed on the outlet listing is not a new manufacturing defect. Support must distinguish a disclosed condition from a fault that arose later.  If the delivered outlet product does not match the listing, report that problem within 14 calendar days after delivery. Keep photographs of the product and the packaging. The support team checks the listing and the received item before arranging a remedy. The 14-day mismatch report window is a separate route from the manufacturing warranty.

Published repair charges  The repair workshop offers a tent pole-section replacement for USD 18 per section and a sleeping-bag zipper-slider replacement for USD 25. These prices cover the named repair work only. Any transport charge is stated in the individual quotation. Other repairs, including a torn tent floor, require a quote after assessment. There is no published flat price for a tent-floor replacement.  A manufacturing fault approved under warranty is handled under the product's warranty terms rather than automatically charged as a paid repair. An accidental tear or wear outside the warranty can still be assessed for paid repair. The workshop tells the customer the scope and price before work begins. The customer must approve the quotation; sending an item for assessment is not approval for an unspecified charge.  Active members receive priority queue handling but pay the same published repair prices. Priority is not a completion guarantee.

An approved manufacturing-defect claim receives a prepaid ground label. For a paid repair, shipping is included only if the individual quotation says so. Warranty decisions apply to the specific damage inspected. A previous approved claim does not guarantee that a different problem will also be covered.

The 14-day mismatch report window is a separate route from the manufacturing warranty. Do not describe it as a 14-day change-of-mind return right. Stock for a replacement outlet product is not guaranteed.

Standard returns for unused gear  The online store accepts ordinary unused gear within 30 calendar days after delivery. Customers must open a return request in the order portal before that window ends. After approval, they have seven calendar days to hand the parcel to the carrier. The request date determines whether the return was opened on time; the carrier acceptance date determines whether the shipping deadline was met.  Keep the original tags attached and include all parts. Trying a jacket on indoors does not count as using it. Washing a garment, taking a sleeping bag camping, or removing a safety seal does count as use. Used products cannot enter the ordinary change-of-mind return process. Hiking boots have a separate fit-trial policy, and damaged products have a separate warranty process. An exception for one product category does not extend the window for other products in the same order.  The warehouse checks the condition before approving the refund. A return request is not itself a refund.
A manufacturing defect discovered later follows the product's warranty process. The seven-day transport-report window does not shorten a separately applicable manufacturing warranty.

Drying and storing outdoor equipment  Dry tents completely before putting them into long-term storage. Moisture trapped in folded fabric can cause mold, odors, and damage to coatings. Brush off loose dirt gently and follow the product's cleaning instructions. Do not use a washing machine or household bleach on a tent. A storage problem is not automatically a manufacturing defect.  Keep sleeping bags dry and store them loosely when space allows. Long-term compression can reduce loft. The product label controls the permitted washing method; different insulation and fabrics may need different treatment. A support agent should not infer washing-machine compatibility merely from the generic sleeping-bag category.  Rechargeable equipment should follow its manufacturer's charging and storage instructions. If a battery is swollen, leaking, or damaged, use the battery-safety process. Generic care advice does not authorize continued charging. This article does not supply a temperature specification for every model, a chemical treatment recipe, or a prediction of remaining battery life.

Reporting delivery damage or the wrong product  Report visible transport damage or a wrong product within seven calendar days after delivery. Keep the outer packaging and photograph the label, packing materials, and affected item. The support team compares those details with the shipment record before approving the claim. If the item is unsafe to use, stop using it while the report is assessed.  An approved wrong-product or delivery-damage return receives a prepaid label. The customer does not pay the ordinary USD 7 change-of-mind label fee for that approved return. The team confirms whether a replacement or another remedy will be provided. A report being opened does not prove replacement inventory exists or establish a delivery date for the replacement.  Damage involving a rechargeable battery follows the separate damaged-battery procedure. Do not put a leaking or swollen battery in an ordinary return parcel even when support is investigating delivery damage. A manufacturing defect discovered later follows the product's warranty process.

answer.answer: For a manufacturing-warranty assessment, you must provide proof of purchase and clear photos so the repair team can assess the seam failure. Your tent falls within the 24-month warranty period for manufacturing defects. A cash refund is not guaranteed; the warranty team chooses repair or replacement after assessment, and support cannot promise a cash refund before that decision.
